name: Generic artificial-intelligence wording (weak)
interpretation: Spelled-out AI language still dominates short summaries. Removing four format words does not solve limited source detail.
review: Broad AI wording without a distinct governance mechanism.

name: AI and generative-AI wording (weak)
interpretation: Short AI-only summaries mix with generative-AI disclosure and deployment language.
review: Wording-driven mixture; not a single governance mechanism.

name: Synthetic media in political communications
interpretation: Synthetic election media and disclosure/prohibition provisions.
review: Recognizable theme preserved after removing format terms.

name: State administration, education and study bodies (broad)
interpretation: State and education vocabulary merges with task-force and reporting language. The former separate task-force cluster is no longer isolated.
review: Representatives emphasize Illinois task forces; the full cluster contains a wider mix of bills.

name: Automated decisions across application domains
interpretation: Employment, lending and other consequential decision tools; shared safeguards require provision-level comparison.
review: Employment and lending examples indicate application domains, not necessarily shared policy requirements.

name: Sexual exploitation and intimate imagery
interpretation: Child sexual abuse material and intimate-image offenses, including synthetic depictions.
review: Coherent issue family, with distinctions between minors and adult nonconsensual imagery.

name: Health services and coverage
interpretation: Care delivery, insurance and health-related AI restrictions, registration and disclosure.

name: Algorithmic pricing and consumer restrictions
interpretation: Top representatives prohibit algorithmic residential rent setting under unfair/deceptive practice rules.
review: Top-five fit is strong but near-identical NY/CO summaries dominate. The larger topic also contains broader consumer provisions.
